title: Even or Odd
statement:
Two friends share a bag of candies. If the number of candies is **even**, they can split it fairly. If it is **odd**, one candy is left over.

You are given an integer **n**. Print `Even` if n is even and `Odd` if n is odd. Remember that zero is even, and negative numbers can be even or odd too.
hints: A number is even when the remainder after dividing by 2 is zero.
In C, C++, Java and JavaScript, `-7 % 2` is `-1`, not `1`. Compare the remainder with 0 instead of with 1.
editorial:
Compute `n % 2`. If it is 0 the number is even, otherwise it is odd. Checking `n % 2 == 1` is a classic bug: for negative odd numbers C++ gives -1, so always test `n % 2 == 0` (or `n % 2 != 0`).

Complexity: O(1).
